name: Syncthing
description: Continuous file synchronisation between devices, peer to peer. The sync protocol is a direct port because devices connect to it, not to a browser.

access.note: Syncthing has no way to be given a web-interface user and password before it starts, and until one is set its interface is a full control surface: any visitor can add their own device, share every synced folder to it, browse the container's filesystem, and set a password that locks the operator out.

retired: Retired 2026-09-22. Syncthing offers no environment variable that sets its web interface's user and password, so a one-image deployment cannot be secured before it first answers — and what it answers with is full control of the sync configuration and a filesystem browser. The race between the operator and everyone else is not a first sign-in this catalogue can promise. Syncthing's own sync protocol is unaffected; the interface is the problem.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: The web interface only; protect it with a password.

ports.name: sync
ports.purpose: The sync protocol, which other devices connect to directly

volumes.purpose: Configuration, keys and the synced folders
